newsitem.title: UK: Argentina $2.0 bln bond to be for 20 years only.
newsitem.headline: Argentina $2.0 bln bond to be for 20 years only.

text.p: Argentina's expected $2.0 billion global bond will all have a 20-year maturity, and not be split into 20- and five-year tranches as originally planned, joint lead manager J.P. Morgan said on Monday.
"There will be no five-year tranche, and a $2.0 billion 20-year global bond is expected on Tuesday," a syndicate manager at J.P. Morgan told Reuters.

"There has been overwhelming investor interest in the 20-year tranche at Argentina's roadshows. It will be the largest global emerging market bond, and will set a new liquid benchmark," the official said.
Spread talk was around 475 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. Merrill Lynch is the other joint lead manager.
The bond was due to be launched on Tuesday, with pricing expected on Wednesday.
Earlier this month, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Argentina would issue a further $1.0 billion in other bonds before March 30.
The Argentine government budgeted $8.0 billion of new debt issues this year. In December 1996 it already raised $2.0 billion for its 1997 financing needs.
